recit.exergue: The start of the Route du Rhum is a unique spectacle, one you have to experience at least once in your life.
p: After 13 days of meeting and sharing with nearly a million visitors, the 115 skippers now find themselves alone, facing themselves and the vastness of the Atlantic Ocean. An ocean that can make lifelong dreams come true, but can also shatter them.
For this 13th edition of the queen of transatlantic races, emotions run high. The last hugs, handshakes and goodbyes, and a few tears wiped away, give way to focus and adrenaline.
All eyes in offshore racing and French sport now turn to the bay of Saint-Malo, where 115 athletes are about to take on the Atlantic Ocean, bound for Guadeloupe.
On land, at sea or comfortably at home, it is a moment suspended in time, when the first lines of new offshore racing legends are already being written.

texte: If you want to watch the start from the coast, please note: the Pointe du Meinga is closed to the public and access to the sites between the Pointe du Grouin and Cap Fréhel is restricted.
Please remember how important it is to protect the natural areas of the coastline, which are remarkable but particularly fragile. Protecting them is everyone’s business!
To do so, adopt the right habits: follow the trail markings, stay on authorised paths and do not enter protected areas.
Volunteers and the police will be on site to inform you, make sure these rules are followed and, if necessary, fine offenders.
qr: Water, food, clothes suited to the weather and ideally a pair of binoculars.
Ideally by bike or on foot, as there will be almost no parking near the headlands.
boutons: To find out more, visit the Protecting the coastline page

texte: The start of the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe is an exceptional spectacle, to be enjoyed from the sea too! Boaters are invited to come and admire the skippers and their boats in a unique setting off Saint-Malo.

To keep this event a celebration for everyone, following the navigation rules and the safety zones is essential. A specific system will be set up to ensure the safety of the skippers, the boaters and all spectators.
We ask everyone to be vigilant and to respect the no-navigation zones, the safety distances and the instructions of the authorities on the water.

items.q: When does the race start, and at what time?
items.r: The race starts on Sunday 1 November 2026 at 1:02 pm, off Saint-Malo, with 115 skippers on the start line.
lien: What is the Route du Rhum?

items.q: How can I watch the start, and from where?
items.r:
There are several ways to enjoy it:

  • on the giant screens of the fan zone, at the village;
  • live on the Route du Rhum's official YouTube channel;
  • on the official website, routedurhum.com;
  • on television, on France 3;
  • from the coast, only in the areas set aside for it: the coastline is a Natura 2000 site, and protecting it is part of the event.

items.q: How many skippers take the start?
items.r: 115 skippers on a single start line, across six classes. The skippers page lets you sort them: first-timers, women, former winners, skippers from the Saint-Malo area or from Guadeloupe, international entrants.

items.q: When is the village open, and at what times?
items.r:
The village is open from Tuesday 20 October to Sunday 1 November: thirteen days of celebration over 70,000 m² around the harbour basins. Exhibitors open at 10 am (at noon on the first day). In the evening, a small part of the village stays open late for partying, until 1 am:

  • Tuesday 20 October: exhibitors from noon to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
  • Wednesday 21 and Thursday 22: exhibitors from 10 am to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
  • Friday 23 and Saturday 24: exhibitors from 10 am to 10 pm, late night from 10 pm to 1 am
  • Sunday 25 to Thursday 29: exhibitors from 10 am to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
  • Friday 30 and Saturday 31: exhibitors from 10 am to 10 pm, late night from 10 pm to 1 am
  • Sunday 1 November, race start day: from 10 am to 5 pm

items.q: Is entry free? Do I need a ticket or a pass?
items.r:
Yes, entry is 100% free, with no ticket: no pass or booking needed, and the village is open to everyone.

There will be systematic bag checks at the entrance.

items.q: Where can I park, and is parking paid?
items.r: Traffic is restricted during the event, car parks are not right next to the entrances, and public parking is paid. The 2026 traffic plan, prices, charging points and closed streets are all on the page.
